sampling_method: Every own-result cell in frame_locations was assigned a contiguous 1-based index in reading order -- location order below, which is page order and, within a page, the order the extracted text presents it. MoCo is typeset in two columns; PyMuPDF's text extraction already resolves left-column-top-to-bottom then right-column-top-to-bottom, confirmed against rendered images for every page checked. A table or figure is taken at the point its float is printed, which on a float-heavy page can precede or follow the body paragraph that first references it: Table 1's scatter-plot-plus-grid floats to the very top of page 6 while the paragraph that introduces it ('Table 1 is the comparison') closes out page 5, and Table 4 floats full-width across the top of page 7, ahead of the column text continuing from page 6 ('...investigate transferabil-|ity of features'). That gives a population of 1..314. The single largest determination this label set rests on: MoCo's transfer-learning tables (2, 3, 5, 6, the LVIS ablation in Appendix A.4, iNaturalist in A.6, the ImageNet fine-tuning table in A.7, and Table A.1) all carry a 'random init.' row and a 'super. IN-1M' row alongside MoCo's own rows, and BOTH are counted as MoCo's own results, not baselines -- because the paper states this as a blanket methodology, not a per-table citation: Sec. 4.2.1's Setup paragraph reads 'The same setup is used for all entries, including the supervised pre-training baseline' (p6/7), Sec. 4.2's opening reads 'our fine-tuning uses the same setting as the supervised pre-training counterpart' and 'random initialization results are provided as references', and Table 3's caption states outright 'All models are implemented by us (Figure 3)'. A 'random init.' row can never be an external citation by construction (there is no other paper to attribute 'we trained from scratch' to), and the supervised-IN-1M row is fine-tuned by the identical pipeline in the identical sentence, so the detection/segmentation/classification number itself -- the thing being labelled -- was produced by this repository even though the upstream ImageNet-supervised checkpoint was not. This is deliberately NOT extended to Table 4: its caption states the opposite outright -- 'The ImageNet supervised counterparts are from the respective papers' -- and its non-MoCo unsupervised columns (RelPos, Multi-task, Jigsaw, LocalAgg) are each some other paper's own published or reproduced number, so only Table 4's three 'MoCo' columns (AP50, AP, AP75) across its four pretraining-data rows are own (12 of its 27 printed cells); the rest are baselines and excluded from the frame by construction, matching this task's brief. Figure 3 (p5) is a line chart with a printed accuracy label at every data point for three series (end-to-end, memory bank, MoCo); all three are the authors' own ablation reimplementations -- 'we implement all of them in the same pretext task' and footnote 2's 'Note the memory bank result of 58.0% reflects our improved implementation of [61]' -- so all 15 printed points are own, confirmed against a zoomed crop of the chart (fig3.png) and against page 5's full image: memory bank runs 50.0/52.0/54.1/56.5/57.8/58.0 at K=256/512/1024/4096/16384/65536, MoCo runs 54.7/56.4/57.5/59.0/60.4/60.6 at the same six K, end-to-end runs only 54.9/56.3/57.3 at K=256/512/1024 (the mini-batch ceiling the text gives for that mechanism). 'MoCo v2' [8] (p6, 71.1% accuracy) is a citation to a separate, later arXiv paper by an overlapping author list, not a number this paper's own repository produced, and is excluded; its parenthetical repetition of '60.6%' is the same printed instance already counted where 60.6% first appears in this location's own earlier sentence, not a new one. Table A.1(a) (p10) reprints Table 5(b)'s entire 2x-schedule grid verbatim, specifically so the reader can compare it beside the new 6x-schedule sub-table (b); each of its 24 cells is counted again as its own printed instance at this new location, matching the standing convention that a value restated at a new place in the paper is a separate reported number (as established for prose restatement in the simsiam.json exemplar) -- here the restatement is a second whole table rather than a sentence, but the principle is the same: a reader or an extractor encounters these 24 numbers again, in a distinct captioned float, on a different page. Every green delta annotation in this paper -- '(+X)', '(-X)' -- is printed beside its absolute in the same cell, so no delta anywhere in the frame is counted separately from its absolute; the handful of prose sentences that restate a delta alone ('up to +0.9 AP50, +3.7 AP...', '3.7 points in AP75dp', 'by up to 0.9 point') all have their absolute printed nearby (the same table or the same paragraph) and are excluded on that basis, per the rule that a delta counts only when no absolute is printed beside it. Genuinely new prose values (not restatements) do count: footnote 2's 54.3% (a reproduction at a different loss/K setting than any chart point), A.7's 77.0% (MoCo IN-1M fine-tuned end-to-end on ImageNet itself, printed nowhere else), and the three restated values in A.4's and A.8's closing paragraphs, each the first prose restatement of a number that had so far only appeared in the table directly above it. random.seed(20260810); random.sample(range(1, 315), 15) drew {1, 3, 25, 28, 49, 57, 139, 166, 182, 197, 214, 216, 244, 295, 305}; each label below records its draw as frame_index. Page images were rendered for pages 5, 6, 7, 8 and 10 (plus two zoomed crops for legibility: a crop of Figure 3 at p5, and a crop of Table 4 at p7), and every row/column attribution among the 14 drawn cells on those pages was checked against them. Table 4 (p7) turned out to hold none of the 15 drawn cells -- it was rendered anyway because its 8-column, 3-metric-group layout could not be resolved reliably from text alone and an accurate total N requires knowing exactly which of its cells are MoCo's own before any draw is made. Conversely, frame_index 244 (Appendix A.4's LVIS ablation table, p9) was NOT confirmed against a page image, to stay within five rendered pages; its 4-row x 6-column grid (clean row labels, no dashes, no merged cells) is structurally identical to Table 5 and Table A.1, both of which were confirmed via image with zero surprises, so it is transcribed from the text dump alone with that stated basis.
